<thought>We have the molecular ion at m/z 127.0997, which likely corresponds to [M+H]⁺. Subtracting the proton mass (1.007276 Da) gives a neutral exact mass of ~126.0924 Da. This mass is consistent with formulas such as C₈H₁₄O (exact mass 126.1040 Da) or C₇H₁₀O₂ (exact mass 126.0681 Da). To distinguish between these possibilities we need NMR data. The next most informative and still inexpensive measurement is the 13C NMR spectrum, which will tell us how many distinct carbon environments are present and whether carbonyl carbons (≈ 170–210 ppm) are observed. This will let us decide between a single‑oxygen aliphatic molecule (C₈H₁₄O) and a dicarbonyl or ester/acid (C₇H₁₀O₂). Therefore I will request the 13C NMR spectrum of the sample.</thought>
